symptoms: Spindle-shaped lesions with grayish-white center and brown margin on leaves and panicle neck node
primary_cause: High nitrogen fertilizer combined with prolonged leaf wetness and warm misty weather
organic_control: Pseudomonas fluorescens foliar spray (0.2%) and bio-fungicide Trichoderma harzianum
chemical_control_guidance: Tricyclazole 75 WP (0.6g/L) or Isoprothiolane 40 EC strictly per CIBRC agricultural dosage
prevention_measures: Use blast-resistant seeds; avoid excess nitrogen; maintain proper plant spacing for airflow

symptoms: Water-soaked yellowish translucent streaks turning into bleached wavy lesions starting from leaf tips
primary_cause: Warm temperature with heavy rain storms causing wounds in plant tissue
organic_control: Fresh cow-dung supernatant spray or copper hydroxide biomixtures
chemical_control_guidance: Copper oxychloride 50 WP (2.5g/L) with Streptomycin sulfate (1g/10L) as advised by state extension officers
prevention_measures: Ensure field drainage; avoid clipping seedling tips during transplanting; balanced NPK nutrition

symptoms: Greenish-grey oval or irregular spots on lower leaf sheaths expanding upward into snake-skin patterns
primary_cause: High plant density with heavy nitrogen top dressing creating humid microclimate at base
organic_control: Foliar spray of Trichoderma viride @ 5g/L or neem cake soil application
chemical_control_guidance: Validamycin 3L (2.5ml/L) or Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole per authorized label
prevention_measures: Maintain proper plant spacing (20x15 cm); reduce urea top dressing; clean weeding of bunds

symptoms: Parallel yellow-orange powdery pustules (stripes) on leaf blades and sheaths
primary_cause: Cool humid mornings with dew retention on canopy and intermittent sunshine
organic_control: Foliar spray of neem-based formulations and Trichoderma harzianum
chemical_control_guidance: Propiconazole 25 EC (1ml/L) or Tebuconazole 250 EC at first flag leaf pustule sighting
prevention_measures: Sow resistant varieties (HD-2967 or PBW-550); timely sowing to escape rust season

symptoms: Scattered round to oval orange-brown powdery pustules randomly distributed across leaf blade
primary_cause: Moderate temperatures with morning dew and warm sunny afternoons
organic_control: Spray fermented buttermilk biomixture and garlic-chili extract
chemical_control_guidance: Tebuconazole 250 EC or Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2g/L upon early detection
prevention_measures: Eradicate alternate weed hosts; seed treatment with Trichoderma viride

symptoms: White talcum-powder like dusting over upper leaf surfaces turning grayish brown with black cleistothecia
primary_cause: Dense crop canopy with high nitrogen fertilizer and shaded cloudy conditions
organic_control: Wettable sulfur (0.2%) or diluted baking soda foliar spray
chemical_control_guidance: Propiconazole 25 EC (1ml/L) or Hexaconazole 5 EC per certified agronomist dosage
prevention_measures: Avoid dense sowing; ensure proper row orientation for sunlight penetration

symptoms: Potato",Concentric ring target-board spots starting on older lower leaves surrounded by yellow chlorotic halo
primary_cause: Soil splash carrying fungal spores during heavy rain spells and warm afternoons
organic_control: Neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%) and Bordeaux mixture (1%)
chemical_control_guidance: Mancozeb 75 WP (2g/L) or Chlorothalonil 75 WP according to authorized plant doctor dosage
prevention_measures: Crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops; straw mulching; stake plants upright off soil

symptoms: Potato",Large irregular dark water-soaked lesions that rot rapidly with white velvety mold under leaves in high humidity
primary_cause: Cool nights (12-15C) followed by humid cloudy days (18-22C) with free water on foliage
organic_control: Trichoderma viride spray and prophylactic bio-copper formulations
chemical_control_guidance: Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (2.5g/L) or Dimethomorph per manufacturer label and expert advice
prevention_measures: Destroy infected crop residue immediately; plant certified disease-free seed tubers

symptoms: Upward leaf curling, stunted growth, puckering of leaves, vein thickening and drop in fruit set
primary_cause: Severe infestation and feeding by Bemisia tabaci whitefly insect vector
organic_control: Spray neem oil (1500 ppm) @ 4ml/L and install yellow sticky traps (20/acre)
chemical_control_guidance: Target whitefly vector using systemic insecticides (Diafenthiuron or Imidacloprid) under extension advice
prevention_measures: Grow barrier crops of maize or sorghum; use silver reflective mulch to repel vector

symptoms: Tomato",Water-soaked decaying blotches on foliage accompanied by rotten purplish-brown tuber surface
primary_cause: Continuous rainfall or sprinkler irrigation keeping canopy wet for >10 hours
organic_control: Bacillus subtilis foliar application and copper-based organic protectants
chemical_control_guidance: Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP applied preventively upon weather blight warnings
prevention_measures: Practice earthing up to 15cm to protect tubers; haulm cutting 10 days before harvest

symptoms: Hard black crusty sclerotia adhering tightly to tuber skin like dirt that won't wash off
primary_cause: Infected seed tubers planted in cold wet soils
organic_control: Seed tuber treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 10g/kg seed
chemical_control_guidance: Boric acid (3%) tuber dip or Pencycuron 250 SC seed dressing before planting
prevention_measures: Use certified disease-free tubers; avoid deep planting in cold soils; crop rotation

symptoms: Angular water-soaked dark brown leaf spots restricted by veins, black lesions on stems (blackarm) and bolls
primary_cause: High temperature and driving rain storms splashing bacterial ooze across plants
organic_control: Spray copper oxychloride (0.25%) with bio-control Pseudomonas
chemical_control_guidance: Copper oxychloride 50 WP (2.5g/L) + Streptocycline (1g/10L) foliar spray
prevention_measures: Delint seed with commercial sulfuric acid; use certified resistant cotton varieties

symptoms: Upward leaf curling, thickening of veins, and small cup-shaped leaf enations on undersides
primary_cause: Explosion of Bemisia tabaci whitefly vector populations in high temperature
organic_control: Spray neem oil (1500 ppm) and protect natural predators like ladybird beetles
chemical_control_guidance: Target the whitefly vector using systemic insecticides strictly per agricultural officer
prevention_measures: Eradicate alternate weed hosts (Abutilon, Xanthium); grow resistant cotton hybrids

symptoms: Tiny reddish-brown to tan pustules (uredinia) on the underside of leaves with yellow chlorotic spots on top
primary_cause: Prolonged leaf wetness (>6 hours) and moderate temperatures during flowering to pod fill
organic_control: Foliar spray of 5% neem extract or Trichoderma harzianum bio-protectant
chemical_control_guidance: Hexaconazole 5% EC (2ml/L) or Tebuconazole 25.9% m/m EC (1.5ml/L) at first symptom appearance
prevention_measures: Early sowing; plant rust-tolerant soybean cultivars; inspect lower canopy leaves weekly

symptoms: Irregular brown spots on stems and pods with diagnostic black spiny setae; premature pod drop
primary_cause: Warm wet humid weather during reproductive growth stages
organic_control: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride and foliar bio-fungicide
chemical_control_guidance: Carbendazim 12% + Mancozeb 63% WP (2g/L) or Azoxystrobin 23% SC foliar spray
prevention_measures: Use disease-free certified seeds; deep summer plowing to bury infested crop residue

symptoms: Circular dark brown spots with prominent yellow halos on leaf surfaces leading to severe defoliation
primary_cause: Prolonged damp soil conditions and intermittent rainy intervals
organic_control: Spray fermented butter-milk extract and neem cake soil incorporation
chemical_control_guidance: Carbendazim 50 WP (1g/L) or Mancozeb 75 WP (2g/L) under agronomist recommendation
prevention_measures: Deep summer ploughing; intercrop with pearl millet or pigeon pea

symptoms: Rotting of seedling collar region at soil surface covered with black powdery fungal mass
primary_cause: High soil temperature with moist planting conditions
organic_control: Seed treatment with Trichoderma harzianum @ 10g/kg seed
chemical_control_guidance: Mancozeb (3g/kg seed) or Thiram seed treatment before sowing
prevention_measures: Avoid deep sowing of groundnut kernels; rotate crops with cereals

symptoms: Third or fourth leaf yellowing, reddening of internal pith with diagnostic white horizontal cross-bands and alcohol odor
primary_cause: Waterlogged fields and planting infected seed setts
organic_control: Drench root zone with Trichoderma harzianum; hot water treatment of seed setts (52C for 30 min)
chemical_control_guidance: Carbendazim sett treatment prior to planting as guided by cane research institute
prevention_measures: Use certified red-rot resistant clones; avoid ratoon crops in infested plots; ensure drainage

symptoms: Emergence of a long, black, curved whip-like structure from the central spindle shoot
primary_cause: Infected seed setts and warm dry winds spreading teliospores
organic_control: Collect whips inside plastic bags before spore release and incinerate
chemical_control_guidance: Dip setts in Propiconazole 25 EC (1ml/L) solution for 15 minutes before planting
prevention_measures: Plant certified smut-resistant varieties; avoid ratoon crops in affected plots

symptoms: Gum exudation on trunk bark near collar region, cracking and rotting of bark and yellowing of foliage
primary_cause: Flood irrigation touching tree trunks and water stagnation around collar
organic_control: Clean scraping of infected bark and pasting with Bordeaux paste (1:1:10)
chemical_control_guidance: Fosetyl-Al 80 WP (2.5g/L) foliar spray or Metalaxyl soil drenching around drip line
prevention_measures: Keep graft union 25-30 cm above soil level; practice double-ring basin irrigation

symptoms: Raised corky blister-like crater lesions with oily margin and yellow halo on leaves, twigs, and fruits
primary_cause: Rain storms carrying bacterial droplets aided by citrus leaf miner leaf wounds
organic_control: Prune infected twigs before monsoon and spray 1% Bordeaux mixture
chemical_control_guidance: Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (2.5g/L) + Streptocycline (1g/10L) foliar spray
prevention_measures: Control citrus leaf miner larvae; install windbreaks around citrus orchard borders

symptoms: Small chlorotic spots turning into linear dark brown to black streaks with grayish sunken centers
primary_cause: High atmospheric humidity, frequent rain showers and dense shaded canopy
organic_control: Cut and burn infected leaves; spray mineral oil emulsion (1%)
chemical_control_guidance: Propiconazole 25 EC (1ml/L) or Carbendazim 50 WP (1g/L) with sticker agent
prevention_measures: Maintain proper spacing (1.8x1.8 m); clear suckers; ensure efficient plantation drainage

symptoms: Yellowing of lower leaves, splitting of pseudostem base, internal vascular discoloration (reddish-brown strands)
primary_cause: Soil-borne chlamydospores persisting in infested soils and contaminated suckers
organic_control: Soil application of Trichoderma viride enriched with neem cake in planting pit
chemical_control_guidance: Corm injection with Carbendazim 2% solution under agricultural officer supervision
prevention_measures: Plant tissue-cultured disease-free plantlets; avoid flood irrigation from infected plots

symptoms: Garlic",Sunken white flecks enlarging into purplish-brown zonate spots on leaves and flower stalks
primary_cause: Humid rainy weather with morning fog followed by warm sunny days
organic_control: Spray 5% neem extract or Trichoderma viride with wetting adjuvant
chemical_control_guidance: Mancozeb 75 WP (2.5g/L) or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC (1.5ml/L) with agricultural sticker
prevention_measures: Use raised nursery beds; maintain wide row spacing for canopy drying; crop rotation

symptoms: Capsicum",Dieback of twigs starting from tip downwards; circular sunken necrotic spots on ripe red pods
primary_cause: High humidity and intermittent rains during fruit ripening stage
organic_control: Seed treatment with Trichoderma harzianum; spray Bordeaux mixture 1%
chemical_control_guidance: Azoxystrobin 23% SC (1ml/L) or Difenoconazole 25 EC (0.5ml/L) per official guidelines
prevention_measures: Collect and burn infected twigs and fruits; seed treatment with Thiram before nursery sowing

symptoms: Drooping of petioles and rachis, yellowing and drying of foliage, brown vascular discoloration in split root
primary_cause: High soil temperature at seedling or flowering stage in low-moisture soils
organic_control: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 10g/kg seed + soil neem cake
chemical_control_guidance: Carbendazim (2g/kg seed) dry seed dressing before planting
prevention_measures: Sow wilt-resistant chickpea varieties (JG-11, JAKI-9218); deep summer plowing; avoid early sowing in hot soils

symptoms: Long elliptical cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions parallel to leaf veins, developing dark olive fungal sporulation
primary_cause: Moderate temperature combined with heavy dew retention and prolonged leaf wetness
organic_control: Foliar spray of Trichoderma harzianum and 5% neem extract
chemical_control_guidance: Mancozeb 75 WP (2.5g/L) or Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC (1ml/L) as per registered label
prevention_measures: Plant resistant maize hybrids; destroy previous crop stubble; avoid excessive overhead sprinkler irrigation

symptoms: Golden-brown to cinnamon powdery pustules scattered profusely over upper and lower leaf surfaces
primary_cause: Cool humid nights followed by mild warm overcast days
organic_control: Foliar application of fermented buttermilk or wettable sulfur (0.2%)
chemical_control_guidance: Propiconazole 25 EC (1ml/L) or Tebuconazole 250 EC at first pustule emergence
prevention_measures: Early planting; plant rust-tolerant maize cultivars; ensure balanced nitrogen-potassium nutrition

symptoms: Irregular dark brown to black necrotic spots on leaves, blossom blight, and tear-stain streaks on immature fruits
primary_cause: High humidity and frequent rainfall during flowering and early fruit development
organic_control: Prune diseased twigs and spray 1% Bordeaux mixture or Trichoderma viride
chemical_control_guidance: Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (3g/L) or Carbendazim 50 WP (1g/L) before flowering and after fruit set
prevention_measures: Prune canopy after harvest for sunlight penetration; collect and burn fallen infected leaves and fruits

symptoms: White superficial powdery coating on inflorescence panicles and tender leaves causing blossoms to drop
primary_cause: Cool cloudy weather with morning mist during flowering season
organic_control: Foliar spray of wettable sulfur (0.2%) or bio-control ampelomyces
chemical_control_guidance: Hexaconazole 5 EC (1ml/L) or Dinocap 48 EC (1ml/L) at panicle emergence and fruit set
prevention_measures: Maintain orchard weed-free; prune overlapping shoots to improve air circulation

symptoms: Translucent oily yellowish spots ('oil spots') on upper leaf surface with dense white cottony down beneath
primary_cause: Warm humid nights with free moisture on foliage for greater than 4 hours
organic_control: Prophylactic foliar spray of Bordeaux mixture (1%) and Bacillus subtilis
chemical_control_guidance: Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (2.5g/L) or Cymoxanil + Mancozeb strictly per CIBRC dosage
prevention_measures: Ensure good trellis aeration; open canopy pruning; avoid water accumulation under vines

symptoms: Circular reddish-brown necrotic spots with distinct dark margins and tiny black pycnidia, berries shrivel into black mummies
primary_cause: Warm wet spring and summer rain splashes carrying fungal ascospores
organic_control: Sanitary removal of mummified berries and spray 5% neem seed kernel extract
chemical_control_guidance: Mancozeb 75 WP (2g/L) or Myclobutanil 10 WP (0.5g/L) per agronomist recommendation
prevention_measures: Destroy mummified fruit clusters on vines and ground; maintain open shoot positioning

symptoms: Striking bright yellow vein network across green leaf lamina, severe stunting and chlorotic unmarketable pods
primary_cause: Rapid spread by whitefly insect vectors (Bemisia tabaci) during warm summer and kharif
organic_control: Deploy yellow sticky traps (25/acre) and spray 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE)
chemical_control_guidance: Target whitefly vector with systemic insecticide (Diafenthiuron 50 WP or Spiromesifen 22.9 SC) per local agronomist
prevention_measures: Grow resistant okra hybrids (e.g. Parbhani Kranti
column13: Arka Anamika); eradicate weed hosts like Malvastrum

symptoms: Sooty black to grayish-brown circular to irregular spots on leaf undersurface causing premature yellowing and defoliation
primary_cause: Warm humid rainy weather with dense plant canopy
organic_control: Foliar spray of Trichoderma harzianum or copper-based bio-protectant
chemical_control_guidance: Carbendazim 50 WP (1g/L) or Mancozeb 75 WP (2g/L) as per label directions
prevention_measures: Maintain proper plant spacing (45x30 cm); clean field sanitation; avoid waterlogging

primary_cause: Warm wet conditions and heavy rain splashes spreading pycnidiospores
organic_control: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride and foliar spray of neem oil (3%)
chemical_control_guidance: Carbendazim 12% + Mancozeb 63% WP (2g/L) or Zineb 75 WP (2g/L)
prevention_measures: Use certified clean seeds; hot water seed treatment (50C for 30 min); collect and destroy rotten fruits

symptoms: Severe reduction in leaf size, leaves become tiny pale soft and bunched together like a broom; plants sterile
primary_cause: Transmitted by leafhopper vector (Hishimonus phycitis) feeding on young shoots
organic_control: Uproot and destroy infected plants immediately; spray neem oil (1500 ppm) with sticker
chemical_control_guidance: Manage leafhopper vector using systemic insecticides (Dimethoate 30 EC or Imidacloprid 17.8 SL)
prevention_measures: Grow barrier crops; early rogueing of infected seedlings in nursery

symptoms: Prominent creamy-white raised pustules or blisters on leaf undersides, swelling and distortion of floral parts ('staghead')
primary_cause: Cool damp rabi mornings with heavy dew deposition
organic_control: Spray garlic extract (2%) or copper oxychloride bio-formulation

prevention_measures: Sow mustard by mid-October to escape infection; seed treatment with Apron 35 SD (6g/kg); crop rotation

symptoms: Concentric target-board brown to black circular zonate spots on foliage, stems, and developing siliquae
primary_cause: Intermittent rain showers followed by sunshine in foggy winter conditions

prevention_measures: Clean cultivation; destroy infected crop debris; use certified healthy seeds

primary_cause: Warm humid rainy weather splashing bacterial ooze through hydathodes on leaf margins
organic_control: Hot water seed treatment (50C for 30 min) and bio-spray with Pseudomonas fluorescens
chemical_control_guidance: Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (2.5g/L) + Streptocycline (1g/10L) foliar spray
prevention_measures: Use disease-free certified seeds; rotate cabbage with non-cruciferous crops for at least 3 years

symptoms: Small circular brownish-black spots with concentric rings on outer wrapper leaves leading to dark velvet sporulation
primary_cause: Cool to moderate temperatures with continuous leaf dampness
organic_control: Foliar application of fermented curd biomixture or Trichoderma viride
chemical_control_guidance: Chlorothalonil 75 WP (2g/L) or Mancozeb 75 WP (2g/L) per authorized recommendation
prevention_measures: Avoid overhead sprinkler watering; wide spacing for air circulation; destroy infected leaves

symptoms: Chlorotic yellowish lesions with circular grayish-brown necrotic centers and dark brown borders on leaf blade
primary_cause: Warm wet monsoon weather with relative humidity above 80%
organic_control: Foliar spray of 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) or Trichoderma harzianum
chemical_control_guidance: Carbendazim 50 WP (1g/L) or Mancozeb 75 WP (2g/L) as per CIBRC directions
